report_title: Decimal block caller adaptation in lexical-parse-integer 1.0.6
selected_scope_from_report:
For an input slice containing the iterator's remaining bytes and an absolute
cursor such that cursor plus the slice length is at most usize::MAX, the adapted
four- and eight-digit callers return successfully for all slice lengths. They
return a value exactly when the next four or eight bytes are ASCII decimal
digits; that value is the positional decimal value. A call returning a value advances
the cursor by the block width. A short or invalid block returns no value and
leaves the cursor unchanged.
limitations_from_report:
These theorems prove the checked safe-read adaptation in the caller harness.
The published callers use lexical-util's Bytes iterator, an unaligned pointer
read, and unchecked iterator advancement. Pinned Aeneas does not translate
those dependencies into usable bodies, so formal equivalence to the published
callers is not established. Native differential tests compare the adaptation
with the release callers at zero and nonzero iterator positions; they are
separate evidence. The helper bodies are decimal specializations of the
published format-generic routines. Other target widths, formats, and public
parsing traits are outside these mappings.
